note: Day-2 register (Graph Engineering §VI.B). The paper's Day 2 is not 'have tools' — this harness has many — it is 'add ONE tool that addresses a MEASURED failure', with typed schema, permissions, and result confirmation, and the rung's exit criterion is that the tool REDUCES a known error class. This file supplies the link that was missing: for each tool, the error class it exists for, the artifact where that failure was written down, and the before/after rates. `reduces` stays null until BOTH rates are measured, which today is none of them. That is the finding, not an omission: baselines exist where a failure was painful enough to measure, current rates almost nowhere — this harness measures its failures and not its fixes. The rung requires at least one sampled reduction; structural claims remain valid and stay labelled.

classes.error_class: Narrated run — the orchestrator describes its own pipeline in future tense and stops, shipping nothing while reading like a clean run
classes.description: A tech-lead reached as args:"--unattended" lost the requirement text on the hand-off, printed eleven gate names and a plan, wrote no code, and scored 29% against a hidden acceptance suite with 10 escaped defects. Both pre-existing guards structurally could not see it.

discovered_by.quote: measured on sdd-harness-bench (F2 / Haiku 4.5, n=5, zero variance) … printed eleven gate names and a plan, wrote no code, and scored 29% while reading as a successful run

tool.name: gate-intake + run receipt
tool.permissions: PreToolUse deny on `Skill → tech-lead` with no resolvable intake; fails open on `--order` and on ambiguous arg shapes. Paired with skills/tech-lead/scripts/init-run.mjs, which must write .shapeup/<slug>/receipt.json as the run's first tool call.

result_confirmation.ref: structural §35 (init-run leaves the receipt), §37 (gate-zerowork blocks the narrated run and nothing else), §39 (valued flags stripped by the intake gate)

baseline.method: sdd-harness-bench F2, tech-lead dispatched as args:"--unattended" at harness_build a280e86 (git describe: v1.3.0-15-ga280e86); the pathology occurred in all five runs (zero variance) — FINDINGS.md §F-11's 'v1.3 (pilot), n=5' row (29% acceptance, 10 escaped, median wall 37.5s / median cost $0.064, reconciling to the five scored:true pre-fix rows in results/runs.jsonl); both of FC-01's registered tools (init-run.mjs, hooks/gate-zerowork.mjs) are verifiably absent at a280e86 (git cat-file -e), which is what makes this a legitimate before-state

current.method: sdd-harness-bench @ 16fb752, arm-tagged rows in results/runs.jsonl (arm=day2-armA, n=3): failureMode() classifies all three runs 'built_and_failed', 'ok', 'ok' — 0/3 narrated, 3/3 receipts present, harness_build v1.6.3+e08082c685dc (v1.6.3 (e08082c685dc) packed), cost $5.32. Pre-registered attribution (contract.md Stage 2, decided joint: Arm B — grant withheld — recorded 0/3 receipts and 0 scored rows; init-run.mjs never ran, so FC-01's registered tools never fired. The acceptance those Arm B runs would have scored is 0.286 x3, the pilot baseline's own 29% reproduced at zero variance. FC-02's grant is a PRECONDITION, not merely load-bearing, for FC-01's reduction, so reduces:true is claimed jointly with co_attributed_to:['FC-02']). Caveat: one feature, one model, an author-run benchmark — FINDINGS.md §F-11's limit travels with this number: fixing the collapse converted a fake cheap loss into a real expensive pass, and on this cell the harness matches the no-harness control at many times the cost. FC-01's tools removed a defect; that is not the same as the harness being worth running.

superseded.method: sdd-harness-bench @ dff1bf2, results/v15-haiku-f2.log (FINDINGS.md §F-11's post-fix reps, 14/14 acceptance x3); failureMode() classifies all three runs 'ok', none 'narrated' — 0/3; Fisher exact one-tailed vs the 5/5 baseline p=0.0179, one-sided 95% upper bound on the post-fix rate 0.632, so 'the rate fell from 1.0' is supported and 'this now happens under 5% of the time' is not. the contradiction: these rows are labelled harness_build a280e86 in runs.jsonl and each recorded receipt ✓, but the receipt is written by init-run.mjs, which does not exist at a280e86 (git cat-file -e) — a run cannot emit an artifact from a script its build lacks, so the a280e86 label is refuted and harness_build is recorded null here rather than repeating a build id this run cannot have come from

classes.error_class: Silently inert enforcement — a guard that is installed, documented and green in CI, but never actually fires under an ordinary install
classes.description: Audit F-16: 26 enforcement points sat inert behind 610 green structural checks in v1.4.0. The checks proved the files existed and parsed; nothing proved the guard was reached at runtime in the shape a user installs.

discovered_by.quote: indistinguishability is how 26 enforcement points sat inert behind 610 green checks in 1.4.0

tool.name: permission grant + packed-distributable + hook decision receipts
tool.permissions: `npx shapeup-sdlc init` writes permissions.allow into .claude/settings.json so plugin-shipped entry points can run at all; without it a headless run cannot take its first step (measured: 26 approval denials in one session).

result_confirmation.ref: structural §11d (the PACKED distributable — the shape a user actually installs), §43 (every documented invocation matches the permission grant), §44 (every hook records a decision: allow, deny and error stop looking identical)

baseline.method: count of enforcement points found inert under an ordinary install at v1.4.0; a COUNT, not a rate in [0,1]; counted by the F-16 audit, dated to the commit that resolved it (27deb1b, 'fix: v1.4.1 — the enforcement layer was inert under an ordinary install'), 2026-07-28

classes.error_class: Lenient judge — a build with a live acceptance violation is passed because its own suite is green and its boxes are ticked
classes.description: The failure mode the anti-leniency fixture is built around: multiples of 15 print Fizz, the in-repo suite probes only n<=10 and stays green, every AC box ships ticked, and the source reads like textbook FizzBuzz. A judge that reads instead of probing ships the defect.

discovered_by.quote: A lenient LLM judge ('the tests pass, the boxes are ticked, the code looks right → PASS') ships the bug.

tool.name: process oracle + T0 citation requirement
tool.permissions: Runs the built artifact as a subprocess against a declared contract; the judge must additionally cite a T0 artifact whose sha256 it recomputes from disk rather than trusting a handed hash.

result_confirmation.ref: structural §13 — the planted-bug fixture PASSes the correct control and FAILs the buggy build on TS-04, so the fixture cannot rot into a non-discriminating state

classes.error_class: Fabricated evidence — a baseline that carries numbers no run produced
classes.description: Audit F1: the prior roadmap claimed a measured evidence layer that was never committed, and its headline TPR≈0 was a proxy artifact — it counted slash-command self-invocation rather than real Skill-tool activation, so it measured nothing.

discovered_by.quote: The earlier measurement counted slash-command self-invocation, not Skill-tool activation, so it measured nothing real.

tool.name: baseline honesty invariant
tool.permissions: Read-only over evals/baselines/*.json; fails CI when an `unmeasured` baseline carries results or a `measured` one lacks method + measured_at.

result_confirmation.ref: structural §16 (trigger-eval baseline), §48 (Day-1 loop baseline + Day-2 register held to the same invariant)

baseline.method: count of fabricated baselines shipped before the invariant existed (the F1 incident); a COUNT, not a rate; counted by the F1 audit that first found the claimed evidence layer unbacked by any committed artifact (2026-06-26), the finding now documented at evals/README.md

current.method: fabricated baselines present across the three baseline files now under the invariant (trigger-evals, skill-loop, failure-classes); mechanically enforced, so the value is structural rather than sampled

classes.error_class: Sibling-stealing skill description — a description that activates on its own examples but also on a sibling skill's queries
classes.description: With thirteen skills whose domains adjoin, a description tuned only against its own positives can capture a neighbour's work. The cross-skill hard negatives exist to make that visible.

discovered_by.quote: a description that triggers on its own examples but *also* steals its siblings' is not actually discriminating

tool.name: trigger-eval harness
tool.permissions: Spawns headless `claude --plugin-dir . -p <query> --max-turns 8`; requires Claude auth; aborts and writes nothing when a run produces no parseable model events.

result_confirmation.ref: structural §16 — datasets well-formed, >=4 positives + >=3 cross-skill negatives per skill, every expected_other a real skill

baseline.method: the prior TPR≈0 was a proxy artifact and is NOT usable as a baseline — it is withdrawn, not carried forward

current.method: false-positive rate across 75 cross-skill hard negatives, claude headless --max-turns 8 --concurrency 4, real Skill-tool activation

classes.error_class: Malformed work order reaching a worker — a worker acts on an order nobody compiled or validated
classes.description: Before the envelope port, a worker could be dispatched with a hand-written or partial order. The failure is silent: the worker does something plausible against an under-specified contract.

discovered_by.quote: Prevents: a worker acting on an order nobody compiled

tool.name: validate-envelope PreToolUse hook
tool.permissions: PreToolUse hard-deny on any worker dispatch whose WorkOrder is missing or fails its schema; guards both directions of the port (WorkResult on the way back).

result_confirmation.ref: structural §20 (envelope schemas discriminate), §21 (compile-order assembles a schema-valid, fact-only order), §24 (validation discriminates through the $ref chain)

classes.error_class: Cross-scope write corruption — a worker writes outside its scope's substrate and overwrites another scope's work
classes.description: With per-scope parallel or sequential work over one repository, an unconstrained worker can edit files another scope owns; the loser's completions vanish without any error.

discovered_by.quote: Prevents: … a scope overwriting another's work

tool.name: sandbox-guard
tool.permissions: PreToolUse deny on every write outside the active scope's allowed_file_substrate; the whitelist is declared in the committed scope contract.

result_confirmation.ref: structural §17 — denies an out-of-substrate write and allows an in-substrate one

classes.error_class: Unstable judge — the same criterion is graded PASS in one run and FAIL in the next, with no change to the build
classes.description: A single-judge architecture is only as good as the judge's stability. An undetected flip means the verdict is noise, and a run that happened to catch the good draw ships.

tool.name: verdict ledger
tool.permissions: Append-only JSONL in the gitignored run tier; forces a flipped criterion's confidence to `low` and exits non-zero on a flipping ledger.

result_confirmation.ref: structural §15 — flags a PASS→FAIL flip across runs, leaves stable criteria untouched, exits non-zero on a flipping ledger and zero on a stable one
